- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model tends to hold too high; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 periods.  
- Model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% immediately.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
